channel.title: AI GridWatch — federal officials and candidates on data centers
channel.description: Every newly cited bill, letter, hearing question or statement on AI data centers by a sitting U.S. senator or a 2026 Senate or House candidate, with the source behind it. From AI GridWatch.

item.title: Suhas Subramanyam (Democratic, VA-10): At a Brookings Institution event, called the current ad hoc, community-by-community approach to data center si…
item.description: At a Brookings Institution event, called the current ad hoc, community-by-community approach to data center siting “short-term profit-driven” and sometimes “predatory”, and called for “a national strategy that puts communities first”: coordinated planning across states, disclosure of development agreements that now carry nondisclosure clauses, and measured rather than projected power and water use. Source: https://www.nextgov.com/modernization/2026/09/do-data-centers-need-national-strategy-puts-communities-first/416137/. Kind: statement. Lean: guardrails. Read 2026-09-22.

item.description: Voted yes on H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, which passed 417-3 (roll call 312). It directs state utility commissions to consider rate designs making data centers with 100 MW or more of peak demand at one site pay the full incremental cost of the generation and grid upgrades they require. A near-unanimous vote: shown on the record, not scored on its own. Source: https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2026/roll312.xml. Kind: statement. Lean: accelerate. Read 2026-09-12.
